author_greeting.ai_message:
Good morning, Sarah. Two things need you today:
[1] Your Maryland Resident Experience Survey closed overnight. 212 responses are in and ready to review.
[2] Your Permit Renewal Feedback draft is scheduled to go out tomorrow and is still unfinished.

Want to start with the results that just came in?

author_cleaning.ai_message:
Before I pull any insights, I ran a data-quality sweep across the 212 responses. A clean dataset is what makes the rest of this trustworthy, so here is what I would fix.

I have left the 14 fast responses unchecked. Excluding someone for answering quickly is a judgement call, not a rule, so that one is yours.
suggested_chips: Tell me more about the speeders

author_speeders.user_query: Tell me more about the speeders
author_speeders.ai_message:
Speeders are respondents who finished in under 25 seconds — below a realistic reading time for six questions. It often means someone clicked through without reading, which flatters satisfaction scores.

But a fast reader answering honestly looks identical in the data, and 14 responses is 7% of your sample. If you want them in, leave that row unchecked before applying.

author_results.ai_message: Here is what the cleaned set says.

author_results_all.ai_message:
Understood — I will use all 212 responses, uncleaned. Bear in mind the duplicates and the eight abandoned starts are still in there, so treat the margins with a little caution.

Here is what the results say:

author_quotes.ai_message: Representative comments about wait times — verbatim and anonymised.

author_more_quotes.ai_message: Three more, on the portal-confusion theme. This one is new this wave — it did not appear at all in the last one.

author_export.ai_message:
Ready to export. The file would carry the cleaned response set, the coded open-text themes, and a data dictionary naming every derived field.

In this demo the download is simulated. In the product this generates a CSV and a tagged PDF summary, both stamped with the cleaning decisions you made.

author_report.ai_message: Here is a one-page summary for your manager. The subject and the headline are editable — click either to change it before sending.

author_send_confirm.ai_message: One confirmation before this leaves the building.
suggested_chips: Yes, send it to my manager

author_saved.ai_message: Saved to your reports. It is ready whenever you want to send it.

author_report_sent.user_query: Yes, send it to my manager
author_report_sent.ai_message:
Sent, and logged to the audit trail under your name. That is job one done.

Ready to finish the Permit Renewal Feedback draft that goes out tomorrow?

author_later.ai_message: No problem — I will remind you before the end of the day. It is due tomorrow, so finishing today keeps the send window intact.

author_draft_status.ai_message:
Here is your Permit Renewal Feedback draft. Six of nine questions are done. Q7 has no answer options, which is the one thing genuinely blocking the send — residents cannot answer it.

I have also flagged Q5 as reading harder than it needs to, with two shorter versions. That one is a suggestion, not a blocker.

author_suggest.ai_message: Q7 asks how easy the renewal was. Based on your own prior permit surveys, here are four options on a consistent scale.

author_manual.ai_message: Go ahead — type your options into the Q7 panel above and I will add them to the survey. Any number works, though four to five is where response quality holds up best.

author_q7_set.ai_message: Q7 is set and the draft is unblocked. Last thing is distribution. This survey went to permit renewers last cycle — about 1,800 contacts. Use the same list?

author_choose_list.ai_message:
You have three saved distribution lists:
[1] Permit Renewers 2025 — 1,800 contacts
[2] All Residents — 12,400 contacts
[3] Service Center Visitors Q1 — 340 contacts

Which one?

author_distribution.ai_message: Distribution set. Last step: choose how the survey actually reaches them.

author_delivery.ai_message: Choose how residents receive this survey. Select as many formats as you like — every one of them is generated from the same single definition, so they cannot drift apart.

author_preview.ai_message: This is what a resident sees.

author_publish_confirm.ai_message: Publishing is the one step here I will not take on my own.

author_published.ai_message: You are all set. The survey is live and on its way.

author_survey_status.ai_message: Here is where it stands right now.

author_new_survey.ai_message:
In the product you would name the survey here and I would draft questions from scratch, then run the same accessibility and plain-language checks you just saw on Q5 and Q7.

This demo focuses on the two jobs already in flight.

author_my_surveys.ai_message:
You have 18 active surveys across six agencies. Marcus sees the same portfolio from the administrator side, where he can ask questions across all of them at once.

This demo focuses on the conversational flow.

__default__.ai_message: Sure — what do you need? You can get back to either of your two tasks any time.
